sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it becomes very, very popular.
sentences.zh: 它变得非常非常流行。

sentences.en: You know, like songs are spreading across the streets of Paris.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像歌曲在巴黎街头传播一样。

sentences.en: This song about the guillotine, you know, people love it.
sentences.zh: 这首关于断头台的歌，你知道，人们很喜欢。

sentences.en: So the guillotine, the word, it begins as a joke, at the guillotine and Guillotin's expense.
sentences.zh: 所以断头台这个词，最初是一个笑话，是以断头台和吉约坦为代价的。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's part of a comic song.
sentences.zh: 它是滑稽歌曲的一部分。

sentences.en: But the truth is that Guillotin is, you know, he's ahead of the curve.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，吉约坦，你知道，他走在了时代的前面。

sentences.en: Because as events will show, his proposal for a beheading machine that will be swift and humane is brilliant for enabling
sentences.zh: 因为正如事件将证明的那样，他提出的那种迅速且人道的斩首机器，对于实现

sentences.en: the two seemingly opposed trends that we've been discussing in this episode to meet and to fuse.
sentences.zh: 我们在本集讨论的两种看似对立的趋势的融合是非常出色的。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, this relish for kind of, you know, a spectacular and salutary display of justice that will be thrilling to people,
sentences.zh: 一方面，这种对某种壮观且有益的司法展示的喜爱，会让人们感到兴奋，

sentences.en: that people can feel simultaneously moral and exciting.
sentences.zh: 人们可以同时感受到道德感和刺激感。

sentences.en: And secondly, the notion that executions should be humane and should repudiate feudalism, should repudiate superstition.
sentences.zh: 其次，这种认为处决应该人道、应该摒弃封建主义、应该摒弃迷信的观念。

sentences.en: So it's both improving.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种改进。

sentences.en: Well, it's improving in every sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它在各个意义上都是一种改进。

sentences.en: It's improving as it works as a spectacular deterrent to crime, but it's improving in that it also, it's more humane, it's clean, it's progressive, it's modern.
sentences.zh: 它既能作为一种壮观的犯罪威慑手段，又在改进，因为它更人道、更干净、更进步、更现代。

sentences.en: So what's not to like?
sentences.zh: 所以有什么不好的呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so an obvious way in which you can make the penal system modern is to get rid of all the shenanigans around executions,
sentences.zh: 所以让刑罚制度现代化的一个显而易见的方法，就是摆脱所有围绕处决的闹剧，

sentences.en: however, their tin-pated spoons and their blood-red robes and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 不管是什么锡制的勺子、血红色的长袍之类的东西。

sentences.en: And to do that requires the delegates in the National Assembly essentially to rule, you know, that the executioner is just a state functionary.
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点，国民议会的代表们本质上需要裁定，你知道，刽子手只是一个国家职员。

sentences.en: He's nothing special.
sentences.zh: 他没什么特别的。

sentences.en: So he's part of a group of people that include Jews and brilliantly include actors who had suffered this kind of civic disabilities under the Ancien Regime
sentences.zh: 所以他属于一群人，其中包括犹太人，还有非常棒地包括了在旧制度下遭受这种公民权利剥夺的演员，

sentences.en: and now they're to be enrolled simply as everyday citizens.
sentences.zh: 现在他们被简单地登记为普通公民。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But even in the final legislation that passes this, they still can't bring themselves to specify executioners.
sentences.zh: 但即使在通过的最终立法中，他们仍然无法下定决心明确提到刽子手。

sentences.en: There's still a kind of superstitious sense in which even to mention the name is cursed.
sentences.zh: 仍然有一种迷信的感觉，仿佛提到这个名字都会受到诅咒。

sentences.en: But the legislation gets passed and so the civic status of Saint-Saëns and other executioners is normalized.
sentences.zh: 但立法通过了，桑松和其他刽子手的公民身份正常化了。

sentences.en: And this is significant because it transforms the figure of the executioner into a servant of the revolution, into someone who is simply, you know, doing a civic duty.
sentences.zh: 这意义重大，因为它将刽子手的形象转变为革命的仆人，转变为一个仅仅是在履行公民职责的人。

sentences.en: Nothing wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 这没什么不对的。

sentences.en: Perfectly rational, perfectly enlightened.
sentences.zh: 完全理性，完全开明。

sentences.en: Perfectly progressive.
sentences.zh: 完全进步。

sentences.en: But having said all that, there are still limits on how far the National Assembly are prepared to go in being progressive.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，国民议会在进步方面所能达到的程度仍然有限。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they're not going to scrap it completely.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不会完全废除它。

sentences.en: I mean, that's pale, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那太苍白了，对吧？

sentences.en: So at the end of May 1791, there is a debate on precisely this and there is a vote on whether the death penalty should be completely abolished.
sentences.zh: 所以1791年5月底，就此进行了辩论，并就是否应完全废除死刑进行了投票。

sentences.en: Robespierre argues that it should.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔主张应该废除。

sentences.en: Votes in favour of its abolition.
sentences.zh: 投票支持废除。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But the majority of delegates disagree and say the death penalty is maintained.
sentences.zh: 但大多数代表不同意，并表示维持死刑。

sentences.en: There is an even more radical proposal than simply abolishing the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 有一个比单纯废除死刑更激进的提议。

sentences.en: I mean, this kind of strikes at the heart of so many assumptions that people are utterly shocked by it, which is that executions, if they are to be maintained and it's decided
sentences.zh: 我是说，这触及了人们如此多的假设，以至于他们感到非常震惊，那就是：如果处决要维持下去——而且已经决定了

sentences.en: that they will be, should be done privately.
sentences.zh: 它们将被维持——那么应该私下进行。

sentences.en: In other words, the salutary quality of it, the way in which executions serve to educate a people, that should be removed.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，那种有益的特质，那种处决用来教育人民的方式，应该被移除。

sentences.en: The removal of a criminal should be like kind of the excision of a cancerous tumour or something.
sentences.zh: 罪犯的移除应该就像切除癌性肿瘤之类的东西一样。

sentences.en: It should just be done neatly, cleanly and privately.
sentences.zh: 它应该干净利落、私下地完成。

sentences.en: People can't get their heads around this idea at all.
sentences.zh: 人们根本无法理解这个想法。

sentences.en: It's kind of howled down.
sentences.zh: 它被大声斥责了。

sentences.en: And so it's agreed that public executions will be maintained and they will be public.
sentences.zh: 所以最终同意维持公开处决，并且它们将是公开的。

sentences.en: But then there is the problem of how, how should these executions take place?
sentences.zh: 但随后出现了如何进行的问题，这些处决应该如何进行？

sentences.en: It's been agreed that there will be only the one method.
sentences.zh: 已经同意只有一种方法。

sentences.en: So that one method needs to be decided upon.
sentences.zh: 所以必须决定那一种方法。

sentences.en: And essentially there are two alternatives.
sentences.zh: 本质上有两种选择。

sentences.en: There's hanging, which is traditionally the way for the poor.
sentences.zh: 一种是绞刑，这传统上是穷人的方式。

sentences.en: As in Britain.
sentences.zh: 就像在英国一样。

sentences.en: Or to be beheaded, which traditionally has been the way for the aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 或者斩首，这传统上是贵族的方式。

sentences.en: And because nothing is too good for the people, it's taken for granted that actually hanging
sentences.zh: 因为没有什么对人民来说是太好的，所以人们理所当然地认为绞刑

sentences.en: is unacceptable, that everyone should now enjoy the rights that traditionally had been the rights of the aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 是不可接受的，现在每个人都应该享受传统上属于贵族的权利。

sentences.en: Partly because of that, but also because it is seen as being quicker.
sentences.zh: 部分是因为这个原因，但也因为它被认为更快。

sentences.en: It's more humane.
sentences.zh: 它更人道。

sentences.en: But the person who raises objections to this, because if everyone is going to be beheaded,
sentences.zh: 但有人对此提出了反对意见，因为如果每个人都要被斩首，

sentences.en: that would potentially require large numbers of people to be dispatched by losing their heads in one go.
sentences.zh: 那可能需要一次性处决大量的人，让他们身首异处。

sentences.en: The person who objects to this is Saint-Saëns, who is no longer the royal executioner, but he's still the chief executioner now of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 提出反对意见的人是桑松，他虽然不再是皇家刽子手，但现在仍是革命时期的首席刽子手。

sentences.en: You know, he presents various arguments against doing it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他提出了各种反对意见。

sentences.en: One is that it requires great skill, which of course Saint-Saëns would argue that.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是这需要高超的技巧，当然桑松会这么说。

sentences.en: But I mean, he's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，他并没有错。

sentences.en: Right, because we've covered executions on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为我们在本播客中讨论过处决。

sentences.en: I think about the Duke of Monmouth.
sentences.zh: 我想到蒙茅斯公爵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Jack Ketch, who had to take eight strokes of the axe or whatever before he managed to get his head off.
sentences.zh: 还有杰克·凯奇，他砍了八斧还是多少下才把头砍下来。

sentences.en: That's a standard, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是个标准，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's always these disastrous scenes on the block where they make a mess of it and it's really bloody and horrible.
sentences.zh: 断头台上总会出现那种惨不忍睹的场面，把事情搞得一团糟，既血腥又可怕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Saint-Saëns was saying that the only way that you could possibly do this is to train up other people, but it takes a long time to do it.
sentences.zh: 桑松说，唯一可行的方法是培训其他人，但这需要很长时间。

sentences.en: Also, there's the risk that if you're using the same axe, the blade will become dull.
sentences.zh: 此外，如果一直使用同一把斧头，刀刃会变钝，这也是个风险。

sentences.en: But above all, he says, it is very, very bloody.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，他说，这实在太血腥了。

sentences.en: So if you remember how Guillotin presented his arguments in favour of it, he's very insouciant about it.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得吉约坦当初是如何论证支持这一点的，他对此表现得非常漫不经心。

sentences.en: He's saying, you know, the blood spurts, the man is no more.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，血喷涌而出，人就没了。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 精彩。

sentences.en: But Saint-Saëns is saying, actually, you know, this is going to be horrific.
sentences.zh: 但桑松说，实际上，这会非常恐怖。

sentences.en: Blood just going everywhere.
sentences.zh: 血会溅得到处都是。

sentences.en: We can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不能那样做。

sentences.en: We need a much more efficient way of sorting this out.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一种更有效率的方法来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So I'll quote you this memorandum that he writes to the National Assembly.
sentences.zh: 所以我引用一下他写给国民议会的这份备忘录。

sentences.en: When there shall be several condemned criminals who will be executed at the same time, the terror created by this form of execution because of the immensity of blood which it
sentences.zh: 当有几名罪犯同时被处决时，这种处决方式所产生的巨大血量，

sentences.en: produces and which it spreads out will give rise to fright and weakness in even the most intrepid of those who remain to be executed.
sentences.zh: 以及它四处飞溅的景象，会让即使是最勇敢的待处决者也会感到恐惧和虚弱。

sentences.en: So in other words, you've got people lining up and there's blood everywhere.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，人们排着队，到处都是血。

sentences.en: So the people at the back of the queue will completely lose it and will not be executed in a decorous way because they'll be shouting and gibbering and behaving badly.
sentences.zh: 所以队伍后面的人会彻底崩溃，无法体面地接受处决，因为他们会尖叫、胡言乱语，表现得很糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this won't be teaching an elevated lesson to the people.
sentences.zh: 这也不会给民众带来什么高尚的教训。

sentences.en: It'll be a shambles, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这会是一场混乱，汤姆。

sentences.en: It'll be rubbish.
sentences.zh: 这会是一团糟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the delegates take all this on board and they think, actually, you know, Dr.
sentences.zh: 所以代表们听取了所有这些意见，他们认为，其实，吉约坦医生的

sentences.en: Guiatan's proposal is not completely mad.
sentences.zh: 提议并非完全疯狂。

sentences.en: So they go to a surgeon, Dr. Antoine Louis, who is permanent secretary to the Academy of
sentences.zh: 于是他们去找了一位外科医生，安托万·路易医生，他是外科

sentences.en: Surgery.
sentences.zh: 学会的常任秘书。

sentences.en: And they say, you know, could you kind of work out what the best kind of machine would be?
sentences.zh: 他们问他，能不能研究出什么样的机器才是最好的？

sentences.en: So Louis goes away and he analyzes, you know, what angle the blade should be at, what would be the most efficient angle for the blade to come down.
sentences.zh: 于是路易去研究了，他分析了刀刃应该处于什么角度，什么样的角度下落最有效率。

sentences.en: He kind of inspects the vertebrae, works out, you know, what's the best way to cut through them and he draws up his report and he hands it back to the National Assembly.
sentences.zh: 他检查了脊椎，研究出切断它们的最佳方式，起草了报告并交回给国民议会。

sentences.en: And Louis' conclusion is, for the certainty of the procedure and to ensure that decapitation
sentences.zh: 路易的结论是，为了确保程序的确定性，并确保斩首

sentences.en: will take place in an instant, in accord with the spirit and the will of the new law, there is no option but to rely on invariable mechanical methods.
sentences.zh: 能在瞬间完成，符合新法律的精神和意志，除了依靠不变的机械方法外别无选择。

sentences.en: So in other words, remove human error, get a machine.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，消除人为错误，用机器。

sentences.en: And so the delegates of the National Assembly go to Dr.
sentences.zh: 于是国民议会的代表们去找吉约坦医生，

sentences.en: Guiatan and say, you know, do you want to take control of this?
sentences.zh: 问他是否想接手这个项目？

sentences.en: You know, he's so offended by this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他对此感到非常冒犯。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to have anything to do with it.
sentences.zh: 他不想和这事有任何瓜葛。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: He turns them down.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了他们。

sentences.en: Because he's been made fun of in the song and stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为他在歌谣里被嘲笑之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's very disgruntled by this.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此非常不满。

sentences.en: He's in a huge sulk and he...
sentences.zh: 他在闹别扭，而且他……

sentences.en: He's in a strop.
sentences.zh: 他在发脾气。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Dr. Louis, he keeps control of the project and he turns to this guy called Tobias Schmidt, who is a German, as his name implies.
sentences.zh: 所以路易医生继续负责这个项目，他转向了一个叫托比亚斯·施密特的人，正如他的名字所暗示的，他是个德国人。

sentences.en: He's a piano maker.
sentences.zh: 他是个钢琴制造匠。

sentences.en: He's also an alcoholic, which you might think is slightly worrying for a man who's going to invent a decapitation machine.
sentences.zh: 他还是个酒鬼，你可能会觉得让一个要发明斩首机器的人酗酒有点令人担忧。

sentences.en: But actually, he does a tremendous job.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他做得非常出色。

sentences.en: It's already one month later.
sentences.zh: 这已经是一个月后的事了。

sentences.en: And Louis then does tests.
sentences.zh: 然后路易进行了测试。

sentences.en: So first of all, he does it on a sheep.
sentences.zh: 首先，他在一只羊身上做了实验。

sentences.en: Then he does it on a calf.
sentences.zh: 然后他在一只小牛身上做了实验。

sentences.en: And then finally, he gets three human corpses and the head's sliced off.
sentences.zh: 最后，他找了三具人类尸体，头被切了下来。

sentences.en: And Louis is absolutely delighted.
sentences.zh: 路易对此感到非常满意。

sentences.en: So to quote him, one is astonished by the force and celerity of its action.
sentences.zh: 引用他的话，人们对它动作的力量和迅捷感到震惊。

sentences.en: And it is now April 1792.
sentences.zh: 现在是1792年4月。

sentences.en: And so the time is ready to try out the execution machine on the first victim.
sentences.zh: 所以是时候在第一个受害者身上尝试这种处决机器了。

sentences.en: And the first victim is a highwayman called Nicolas-Jacques Pelletier, who had committed armed robbery in October 1791.
sentences.zh: 第一个受害者是一个叫尼古拉-雅克·佩尔蒂埃的拦路强盗，他在1791年10月犯下了武装抢劫罪。

sentences.en: He'd been sentenced to death in December, has been in prison awaiting his execution.
sentences.zh: 他在12月被判处死刑，一直被关在监狱里等待处决。

sentences.en: And he is the person who, on the 25th of April 1792, is led out to the Place de la Greve, the traditional place of execution, where there is standing a peculiar looking machine.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个在1792年4月25日被带到格列夫广场（传统的处决地点）的人，那里矗立着一台看起来很奇怪的机器。

sentences.en: And the news has got out.
sentences.zh: 消息已经传开了。

sentences.en: So there's a large crowd to witness it.
sentences.zh: 所以有大批人群来见证这一幕。

sentences.en: Pelletier is led up to the scaffold by Saint-Saëns.
sentences.zh: 佩尔蒂埃被桑松带上断头台。

sentences.en: Saint-Saëns cuts off his hair, ties Pelletier's hands behind his back, straps him down onto a board, pushes him out so that his neck is exposed to the blade, pulls on a rope.
sentences.zh: 桑松剪掉他的头发，把佩尔蒂埃的双手反绑在背后，把他绑在木板上，推出去让他的脖子暴露在刀刃下，然后拉动绳子。

sentences.en: The blade slices down.
sentences.zh: 刀刃切下。

sentences.en: The head vanishes into a sack.
sentences.zh: 头掉进了袋子里。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: It's all over.
sentences.zh: 一切都结束了。

sentences.en: And the crowd are completely bewildered.
sentences.zh: 人群完全困惑了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Gutting for the crowd, who've been queuing there probably for hours.
sentences.zh: 这对人群来说很扫兴，他们可能在那里排了几个小时的队。

sentences.en: And it's done and dusted in seconds.
sentences.zh: 结果几秒钟就完事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So a witness, very disgruntled eyewitness, wrote, from the first point of contact to the last, there is no distance.
sentences.zh: 所以一位目击者，一位非常不满的目击者写道，从接触的第一点到最后一点，没有任何距离。

sentences.en: It is an indivisible point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不可分割的点。

sentences.en: The blade falls and the patient no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 刀刃落下，病人就不复存在了。

sentences.en: The patient.
sentences.zh: 病人。

sentences.en: Isn't that so interesting, the kind of medical metaphor?
sentences.zh: 这种医学隐喻不是很耐人寻味吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because it is like a surgical operation.
sentences.zh: 因为它就像一场外科手术。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And when Guillotin first proposed this machine, he commissioned illustrations, which show
sentences.zh: 当吉约坦首次提出这台机器时，他委托制作了插图，图中显示

sentences.en: a priest ministering to the person who's about to have his head cut off, as though, you know, tending a deathbed or something like that.
sentences.zh: 一位牧师在为即将被砍头的人进行临终关怀，就像在照料临终者一样。

sentences.en: And this idea that it is, it's like having an operation.
sentences.zh: 这种认为它就像做手术的想法。

sentences.en: It's smooth.
sentences.zh: 它很平滑。

sentences.en: It's clear.
sentences.zh: 它很清晰。

sentences.en: It's kind of dignitas.
sentences.zh: 它有一种尊严感。

sentences.en: And I think that the ambivalence is suggested by the name which the machine comes to be given, which of course is guillotine.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种矛盾心理体现在这台机器后来被赋予的名字上，当然就是断头台（guillotine）。

sentences.en: So it's initially called a Louisette, but the association of Guillotin's name with this kind of contraption is too strong.
sentences.zh: 它最初被称为“路易塞特”，但吉约坦的名字与这种装置的联系太紧密了。

sentences.en: And so it ends up being named after him.
sentences.zh: 所以它最终以他的名字命名。

sentences.en: And it's reflective of the way, I think, in which it comes to have its own mythology very, very rapidly.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了它非常迅速地形成了自己的神话。

sentences.en: It's quick.
sentences.zh: 它很快。

sentences.en: It's efficient.
sentences.zh: 它很高效。

sentences.en: It's humane, certainly relative to what had gone before.
sentences.zh: 它很人道，当然是相对于以前的方式而言。

sentences.en: But it is also very, very bloody.
sentences.zh: 但它也非常、非常血腥。

sentences.en: And as Saint-Saëns had pointed out, the more criminals who are executed in one go, the more bloody the spectacle will become.
sentences.zh: 正如桑松指出的那样，一次性处决的罪犯越多，场面就会变得越血腥。

sentences.en: And so, as we said, this fusion between the traditional spectacle and the new way of doing things.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我们所说，这是传统奇观与新做事方式的融合。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The guillotine kind of exemplifies it.
sentences.zh: 断头台在某种程度上体现了这一点。

sentences.en: But Tom, isn't it also that it's the fact that you can do so many people in one go?
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，难道不是因为它能一次性处决那么多人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the uniformity of it is what is chilling.
sentences.zh: 而且它的统一性才是最令人不寒而栗的。

sentences.en: So the previous way of execution, as unbelievably horrific as that was, there was something about it that kind of respected you as an individual.
sentences.zh: 以前的处决方式，尽管极其恐怖，但其中某种程度上还尊重你作为一个个体的存在。

sentences.en: You are Calas or Damien or whatever his name is, and you are brought out.
sentences.zh: 你是卡拉斯或达米安，或者不管他叫什么名字，你被带出来。

sentences.en: And this whole day is about you.
sentences.zh: 这一整天都是关于你的。

sentences.en: You're at the center of it.
sentences.zh: 你是中心。

sentences.en: And it's specific to you.
sentences.zh: 这是针对你个人的。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not sure that's a great consolation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不确定这算不算什么大的安慰。

sentences.en: No, of course not.
sentences.zh: 不，当然不是。

sentences.en: It's not a great consolation.
sentences.zh: 这算不上什么大的安慰。

sentences.en: But with this, isn't it that the ominous thing about it, especially looking back from the 21st century, is that you can polish off dozens, hundreds of people in a day or two.
sentences.zh: 但有了这个，难道最不祥的事情不是——特别是从21世纪回望时——你可以在一两天内干掉几十、几百人吗？

sentences.en: And they're just numbers, people in a queue.
sentences.zh: 他们只是数字，队列中的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're anonymous.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们是匿名的。

sentences.en: They're anonymous.
sentences.zh: 他们是匿名的。

sentences.en: It's the anonymity of it that I think is the frightening thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我认为这种匿名性才是最可怕的事情，不是吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that what?
sentences.zh: 不是什么？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But it also, of course, forms its own spectacle.
sentences.zh: 但它当然也形成了它自己的奇观。

sentences.en: The spectacle of a large line of people being beheaded is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 一大排人被斩首的奇观是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: No one's ever seen anything like it before.
sentences.zh: 以前没人见过这样的场面。

sentences.en: And so even though the theatrical quality of executions, as you said, has been banned, there is a new theatricality about this.
sentences.zh: 所以即使正如你所说，处决的戏剧性已被禁止，但这其中产生了一种新的戏剧性。

sentences.en: And you get larger and larger crowds for it.
sentences.zh: 而且观看的人群越来越多。

sentences.en: And so the guillotine is moved from the Place de la Grève to ever larger venues.
sentences.zh: 所以断头台从格列夫广场搬到了更大的场地。

sentences.en: And it will end up being put in what today is the Place de la Concorde, but comes to be named the Place de la Revolution after the abolition of the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 它最终被放置在今天被称为协和广场的地方，但在君主制废除后，它被称为革命广场。

sentences.en: And there it comes to stand as the kind of the defining emblem of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 在那里，它成为了革命的标志性象征。

sentences.en: And people want to watch it.
sentences.zh: 人们想看它。

sentences.en: So it has become a spectacle kind of despite itself.
sentences.zh: 所以它在某种程度上违背初衷地成为了一种奇观。

sentences.en: And that's why it's so appropriate that Saint-Saëns, who had been the royal executioner, is now the executioner operating for the execution of the enemies of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么桑松——曾经的皇家刽子手，现在成为执行革命敌人处决的刽子手——是如此的恰如其分。

sentences.en: And it's why even though you no longer have female aristocrats gathering at private windows to gawb, you do have women in particular who become notorious for the delight they take
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么尽管不再有女性贵族聚集在私人窗户前窥视，但确实有一些女性因她们从死亡奇观中获得的快感而臭名昭著。

sentences.en: in the spectacle of death.
sentences.zh: 在死亡的奇观中。

sentences.en: And these, of course, are the tricoteurs, the women who knit.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些就是“编织女”，也就是那些织毛衣的妇女。

sentences.en: These are the women from the market who had gone and seized the king and queen from Versailles in 1789 and who have particular privileges as a result.
sentences.zh: 这些是来自市场的妇女，她们在1789年从凡尔赛抓住了国王和王后，因此拥有特殊的特权。

sentences.en: They get the front row.
sentences.zh: 她们坐在前排。

sentences.en: So the sense of rupture is obviously very, very profound.
sentences.zh: 所以这种断裂感显然是非常、非常深刻的。

sentences.en: But so too, beneath the seeming show, there are continuities as well.
sentences.zh: 但同样，在表面之下，也存在着连续性。

sentences.en: And that, I guess, is one of the reasons why the guillotine is the kind of perfect symbol of the revolution, really.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是为什么断头台是革命的完美象征的原因之一，真的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Tom, that was absolutely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这太令人着迷了。

sentences.en: So the guillotine has been set up.
sentences.zh: 所以断头台已经架好了。

sentences.en: The blade has been sharpened.
sentences.zh: 刀刃已经磨好了。

sentences.en: The tumbrils are rattling through the streets.
sentences.zh: 囚车正吱呀作响地穿过街道。

sentences.en: And there is going to be a steady stream of customers for Madame Guillotine because, as we discussed last time, Tom, France is going to war.
sentences.zh: 断头台夫人将迎来络绎不绝的顾客，因为正如我们上次讨论的那样，汤姆，法国要开战了。

sentences.en: If you thought this episode was bloody, there is a lot more blood to come tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这一集已经够血腥了，明天还有更多血腥的内容。

sentences.en: So you can listen to that episode right now if you're a member of the Rest is History Club.
sentences.zh: 如果你是“历史余韵”俱乐部的会员，现在就可以收听那一集了。

sentences.en: If not, if you prefer the old-fashioned ways of the wheel and the axe, then you'll just have to wait.
sentences.zh: 如果不是，如果你更喜欢车裂和斧头这种老派方式，那就只能再等等了。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Happy hour, too.
sentences.zh: 还有欢乐时光。

sentences.en: Happy hour, too.
sentences.zh: 还有欢乐时光。
